newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-VOGTS SLAMS MANAGERS FOR WINTER BREAK PLANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VOGTS SLAMS MANAGERS FOR WINTER BREAK PLANS.

text.p: Germany coach Berti Vogts warned club managers on Tuesday that the quality of the national side would suffer if they did not accept his plans to shorten the Bundesliga's annual winter shutdown.

Vogts has won backing from the German Soccer Federation (DFB) to shorten next season's break so the league programme finishes earlier, giving him more time to prepare with the national squad for the World Cup in France.

But club managers agreed at a meeting on Monday they wanted the shortened winter break to be a one-off, arguing there was no point trying to play games when the weather was at its worst and then finishing up when conditions were still ideal.

"We've worked out a shortened winter break for the 1997-98 season. If this is reversed in 1998-99, then it's the national team which will suffer most," Vogts told a news conference to announce his squad for next week's friendly against Israel.

Vogts said medical experts were also in favour of a shorter winter break. It would ease fixture congestion in the second half of the season, making national team players less liable to injury and tiredness.

"The fans have a right to see the best players in the Bundesliga," Vogts said. "We are the only major league which tries to take players from a standing start to peak fitness twice a season, in summer and in winter."
